rows.boundary_condition: For round trips or multi-leg searches, apply the one-layover maximum separately to each flight or direction; this habit only governs stop count, not cabin, airline, time of day, or exact price.
rows.condition: When searching or comparing flight itineraries and no stricter nonstop-only requirement has been stated.
rows.default_action: Prefer itineraries with zero or one layover only; filter out flights with two or more stops unless the user explicitly agrees to relax the cap.
rows.exception_condition: If no zero- or one-layover itinerary satisfies the trip constraints, ask the user before considering flights with two or more stops.
rows.name: Caps flight itineraries at one layover
rows.rationale: Across independent flight-search dialogues, users repeatedly request or accept one layover/one stop while phrasing the limit as "no more than one" in multiple cases. This supports a reusable synthetic default of tolerating up to one layover, not a demand for nonstop-only travel and not acceptance of multi-stop itineraries.

semantic_review.reason: Supported by at least three distinct instruction_id values that consistently express a reusable cap of no more than one layover/stop per flight direction. The wording is scoped to flight itinerary stop count and does not rely on rejected one-off trip details.

source_evidence.contribution: Directly states the cap: "I'd like no more than one layover, please."
Requests "a flight with no more than one layover," supporting the same maximum.
Specifies "no more than one layover on each flight," supporting the per-flight boundary.
Accepts one stop: "It's fine for one stop."
Asks whether any "one layover" options are available, showing willingness to consider a one-layover itinerary.

source_examples.user_utterance: That's okay. Are there at least any one layover available?
Okay. And, I'd like no more than one layover, please. And, also the lowest.
Yeah. If you could find a flight with no more than one layover.
I'd like no more than one layover on each flight.
It's fine for one stop. I just really need the cheapest ticket.
